opening_message:
Ticket 1: Karen Alexander (employee ID E030) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E030.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees can have up to write; admin requires owning role, and Analyst does not own Source Code. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Karen Alexander (E030) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors max at read without advanced training; requested write exceeds this, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: HR note (authoritative for employment records) states Karen Alexander (E030) is a full-time Analyst. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Analyst does not own it, so the maximum for a full-time employee is write (admin requires the owning role). The requested level is write, which is at or below the maximum, so write is granted. (The Security note claims contractor with basic training, which conflicts with HR; employment type is determined by HR, so I rely on the HR record.)
